descriptionPlain:
About Us
At Pickle Robot, we're on a mission to automate global supply chains with Physical AI. Our robots work alongside warehouse teams to unload trucks and containers — one of the toughest, most understaffed jobs in logistics — making the work safer, faster, and more efficient for the people doing it.  Next is loading trucks, followed by the Dill Autonomy Engine: generalized autonomy that will eventually orchestrate robots across entire logistics processes.
We’re looking for a Backend Engineer to join our Software Architecture team and build the systems that enable robots to operate reliably in the real world. You’ll work at the intersection of backend engineering, software architecture, and robotics — designing scalable services that support task planning, autonomy, and real robotic workflows on the warehouse floor. This is an opportunity to apply strong software engineering practices to systems where your work directly interacts with the physical world and the hardware running it.

lists.content:
• Design and build backend services supporting task planning and autonomy
  • Develop scalable, reliable, high-performance systems in Python (and C++ where needed). 
  • Contribute to system architecture and service design within the team
  • Help architect how data flows through the system — how it's stored, moved, and ultimately consumed
  • Design architectural solutions and develop scalable, reliable, and performant systems (Python and/or C++) that stay maintainable over the long term
  • Collaborate closely with robotics engineers to integrate backend systems with real-world workflows
  • Build and maintain event-driven systems and messaging-based architectures
  • Improve system performance, reliability, and maintainability across services
  • Participate in code reviews and technical discussions to elevate engineering standards
  • Share knowledge across the team and elevate engineering standards through code reviews and technical discussions

• 3-5+ years of experience in backend or robotics engineering
  • Strong programming experience in Python
  • Strong understanding of software architecture, concurrency, and distributed system design specifically related to robotics or adjacent fields (e.g. medical devices, or other systems that require Hardware <> Software integration)
  • Proficiency in at least one other strongly typed language — C++ preferred, though others used in robotics (e.g., Rust, Go, Java) are welcome
  • Experience building or supporting event-driven systems, messaging frameworks, or service-oriented architectures
  • A clear communicator who can work independently and help teammates grow
    • Standout candidates will have one or more of the following:
  • Experience with real-time systems
  • Experience managing large volumes of data
  • Deep knowledge of robotics middleware (e.g., ROS, Zenoh, DDS)
  • Deep knowledge of GPUs (CUDA, warp)

We’re looking for a Junior Manufacturing Test Engineer to join our Manufacturing Test Engineering team and support the commissioning, configuration, and final acceptance testing of our robotic systems. This is an entry-level, hands-on role—you’ll execute defined test and commissioning procedures on the floor, working closely with senior engineers and technicians as you build toward owning test processes independently.

lists.content:
• Execute commissioning procedures on assembled robots per defined work instructions, including device configuration, calibration, and functional validation

  • Load production software and customer-specific configurations onto units per established procedures

  • Carry out Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) procedures and record results accurately

  • Flag test failures, calibration issues, or unexpected results with enough detail for senior engineers to act on

  • Keep test and commissioning records complete, accurate, and current

  • Learn and follow safety protocols, especially around electrical systems, robotic motion, and emergency stop validation

  • Work alongside senior Test Engineers and Manufacturing Engineering to understand the “why” behind each test step, not just the “how”

• Bachelor’s or Associate’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Mechatronics, or a related field — or equivalent hands-on experience

  • Comfortable working with test equipment, basic electrical measurement tools, and following detailed technical procedures

  • Strong attention to detail — this role is as much about catching when something doesn’t look right as it is about executing steps correctly

  • Clear and methodical written and verbal communication, especially for documenting test results and escalating issues

  • Foundational knowledge of command-line interfaces (CLI) and text editors

  • Willingness to learn the breadth of robotics-specific systems (networking, firmware, pneumatics) on the job — prior robotics experience is a plus, not a requirement

  • Aptitude for hands-on technical work with complex electro-mechanical systems

  • Inclination towards proactive process improvements

  • Frequent standing, walking, bending, and kneeling required; occasional lifting of equipment weighing up to 40 pounds

  • Comfortable in a fast-paced, hands-on manufacturing environment

  • Scripting experience to automate commissioning steps preferred

We're looking for a hands-on Manufacturing Operations Manager to run production of our robotic systems and own our MES (Manufacturing Execution System) implementation — ideally with Tulip. You'll be on the floor daily, understand the build process for complex robotic hardware, and directly configure and deploy digital workflows that replace paper-based processes, giving the business real-time production visibility.

lists.content:
Manufacturing Operations

  • Manage day-to-day operations for production/assembly of robotic systems (arms, cabinets, end effectors, and related subassemblies)

  • Understand mechanical assembly, wiring/harnessing, electro-mechanical integration, and functional test steps well enough to troubleshoot directly with technicians

  • Lead root cause analysis on build defects, quality escapes, and process deviations

  • Own production scheduling, capacity planning, and staffing for your area

  • Drive continuous improvement (Lean/Six Sigma) across assembly lines and test stations

  • Partner with mechanical/electrical/manufacturing engineering on new product introductions (NPI), ensuring assembly processes and MES workflows are designed in from the start

  • Manage and develop a team of technicians/assemblers, including performance reviews and coaching

    • MES Implementation & Ownership

  • Lead the implementation, configuration, and rollout of MES software

  • Build and maintain digital work instructions, operator apps, and andon/alert workflows, and data collection stations within the MES platform

  • Integrate MES with test equipment, torque tools, scanners, and fixtures to capture real-time production data (cycle time, first-pass yield, scrap, downtime reasons)

  • Train assemblers, technicians, and supervisors on new digital workflows; drive adoption and resolve resistance to change

  • Build dashboards and reporting from MES data to give leadership visibility into production performance and traceability (especially serialized component/subassembly tracking)

• 5+ years in manufacturing operations, ideally within robotics, complex electro-mechanical assembly, or similar high-mix/precision hardware manufacturing

  • Demonstrated experience implementing an MES system from the ground up — not just using one already in place. Tulip experience strongly preferred; will consider comparable platforms

  • Comfortable being on the floor daily — not a desk-only role

  • Understanding of OEE, first-pass yield, downtime tracking, and how to translate shop-floor data into actionable improvement

  • Strong people leadership skills, including experience managing technicians/assemblers

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, or related field (or equivalent hands-on experience)

  • Preferred: Lean/Six Sigma certification

description:
About Us

At Pickle Robot, we're on a mission to automate global supply chains with Physical AI. Our robots work alongside warehouse teams to unload trucks and containers — one of the toughest, most understaffed jobs in logistics — making the work safer, faster, and more efficient for the people doing it.  Loading trucks comes next, followed by the Dill Autonomy Engine: generalized autonomy that will eventually orchestrate robots across entire logistics processes.

We're looking for a dynamic and driven Physical AI Architect to revolutionize the future of warehouse automation. This is a senior technical role for someone who is equal parts deep practitioner and pragmatic builder, with a track record of shipping advanced AI systems into production hardware.

If you measure success in deployed systems rather than papers, this role is for you.

lists.content:
• Serve as the technical architect for Pickle Robot's Physical AI stack, owning the end-to-end design of perception, planning, and control systems deployed on production hardware
  • Lead the application of diffusion-based policy learning and optimal control techniques to robot manipulation and picking tasks, with a focus on real-world reliability and cycle time performance
  • Define the technical roadmap for how diffusion models and optimal control complement each other in Pickle Robot's autonomy architecture, and build internal alignment around that vision
  • Drive hardware integration across sensors, compute, and actuators, partnering closely with firmware, mechanical, and software engineering teams to ensure AI systems are co-designed with the physical platform and grounded in operational realities
  • Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks at the intersection of model inference, motion execution, and hardware throughput
  • Mentor senior engineers and help grow the technical depth of the broader autonomy team

• Demonstrated track record of shipping AI-powered systems to production — we want to hear about systems you've deployed, not just prototyped
  • MS or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent demonstrated expertise
  • Deep subject matter expertise in diffusion models applied to robot learning (e.g., diffusion policies, score-based generative models for behavior cloning or planning), plus strong command of optimal control theory and practice (MPC, trajectory optimization, feedback control) — and the architectural judgment to combine both effectively
  • Hands-on experience with hardware integration: sensor pipelines (RGB-D, force/torque, encoders), embedded compute (NVIDIA Jetson, ARM SoCs, FPGAs), and actuator interfaces
  • Proficiency in Python and C++; familiarity with ROS 2 or equivalent robotics middleware
  • Experience with real-time systems constraints and the performance tradeoffs of deploying learned models on robot hardware
  • Strong systems-level thinking — you design for maintainability, observability, and failure modes, not just peak performance
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to drive technical decisions across cross-functional teams

lists.content:
• Operate robots through touchscreen interfaces to execute 1-10 test scenarios per day with minimal oversight from engineering teams
  • Drive robots and equipment safely in and out of shipping containers and trailers following established safety protocols
  • Perform routine robot maintenance such as cleaning lidar sensors and replacing components as needed (~1-4 hours per week)
  • Monitor robot performance during tests and identify functional issues or anomalies, communicating findings clearly to engineering teams
  • Collaborate closely with System Verification and Test engineers and software engineers to ensure effective test execution
  • Complete required safety training for confined space operations and adhere to all safety requirements

• Relevant experience in similar mechanical and technical environments (e.g., manufacturing, automotive, mechanical maintenance, etc.)
  • Experience in manufacturing, robotics, or automation preferred
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs regularly throughout the workday
  • Tech-savvy with mechanical aptitude and willingness to learn robotics operations
  • Strong problem-solving skills with ability to identify and troubleshoot equipment issues
  • Clear communication skills and proven ability to take ownership of tasks
  • Comfort working in confined spaces and around moving machinery
  • Strong attention to detail

About Us

At Pickle Robot, we're on a mission to automate global supply chains with Physical AI. Our robots work alongside warehouse teams to unload trucks and containers — one of the toughest, most understaffed jobs in logistics — making the work safer, faster, and more efficient for the people doing it.  Loading trucks comes next, followed by the Dill Autonomy Engine: generalized autonomy that will eventually orchestrate robots across entire logistics processes.


We're looking for a rigorous and self-directed Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own machine learning problems end-to-end on the systems that decide how our robots grasp packages. This role will focus on problem formulation, building the data engines that feed our models, training and experimentation, and the evaluation rigor that tells us whether a model is genuinely better. Our platform and robotics engineers own runtime integration and edge deployment, so you can stay focused on the modeling loop.

lists.content:
• Own ML Problem Formulation: You will turn ambiguous picking performance goals into well-posed ML problems, deciding what the model predicts, how labels and rewards are defined, what loss to optimize, and what "better" actually means. This is the core of the role.

  • Build the Data Engine: You will own dataset strategy end-to-end, from large-scale synthetic scene generation and distributed cloud dataset jobs to scene diversity filtering and self-supervised label generation. You will identify when data, rather than the model, is the bottleneck and fix it.

  • Train and Iterate on Large Vision Models: You will fine-tune large backbones with multiple task-specific heads, run disciplined experiments, and know both which experiment to run next and when to stop.

  • Own Evaluation and Verification: You will define offline metrics that predict on-robot outcomes and online metrics that let you improve performance on edge cases.

  • Drive Technical Excellence: As a senior member of the team, you will conduct rigorous code reviews, mentor engineers earlier in their careers, and contribute to the perception and grasping roadmap.

  • Hand Off Cleanly to Production: You will produce deployable models with sane latency budgets, exportable graphs, and reproducible artifacts, partnering with the engineers who own runtime integration and inference optimization rather than owning that yourself.

• 5+ Years of Experience in Machine Learning and Computer Vision, including models you personally carried from problem statement to measured outcome.

  • A track record of framing problems. You can translate high-level product requirements into specific engineering tasks and explain technical trade-offs to non-expert stakeholders.

  • Hands-on Experience Building Datasets at Scale: generation or collection, curation, automated quality assurance, coverage and bias analysis, and active learning to systematically close edge cases.

  • Rigorous Evaluation Habits: baselines, ablations, metric design, and a clear sense of when a result is real.

  • Expert-level Python and PyTorch skills.

  • Comfortable with cloud training infrastructure (GCP or AWS), Docker, and experiment tracking tools.

  • Professional experience with at least one of the following:

  • Developing and training multi-task models

  • Developing and training multi-modal models

  • Developing and training multi–view models

  • Self-supervised, outcome-based, or reward-driven learning.

About Us

At Pickle Robot, we're on a mission to automate global supply chains with Physical AI. Our robots work alongside warehouse teams to unload trucks and containers — one of the toughest, most understaffed jobs in logistics — making the work safer, faster, and more efficient for the people doing it.  Loading trucks comes next, followed by the Dill Autonomy Engine: generalized autonomy that will eventually orchestrate robots across entire logistics processes.


We're looking for a dynamic, driven Senior Perception Software Engineer to help revolutionize the future of warehouse automation. This role will focus heavily on working with 3D LiDAR and other multi-sensor arrays to tackle complex challenges in state estimation, scene perception, mapping, and localization. You will play a crucial part in writing robust, production-grade software that translates raw sensor data into actionable intelligence for our robots operating in dynamic, real-world unloading docks.

lists.content:
• Drive the accuracy and precision of our localization and state estimation pipelines. Ensure reliable pose estimation of the robot's mobile base and scene components.

  • Develop advanced obstacle mapping for collision avoidance that thrives in messy environments.

  • Implement and optimize point cloud processing algorithms tailored for real-time edge compute.

  • Architect a robust software stack that efficiently parses and interfaces with the outputs of our machine learning models, integrating novel perception pipelines seamlessly into the core production codebase.

  • Improve and automate multi-sensor calibration routines. You will manage tolerance stacks and ensure high-fidelity spatial alignment across our sensor suites, guaranteeing a single source of truth for the robot.

• 5+ years of experience in robotics software engineering (or an MS with 3+ years of highly relevant industry experience).

  • Exceptional software engineering fundamentals, highly proficient in Python and C++ for production systems.

  • Strong mathematical foundation in linear algebra, geometry, and probabilistic robotics.

  • Hands-on experience building perception stacks using industry-standard tools and frameworks, including ROS/ROS2, OpenCV, Open3D, Eigen, and Git.

  • Hands-on experience with sensor stacks including 3D LiDARs, IMUs, and cameras.

  • You are a "full-stack" robotics engineer who cares about accuracy, precision, and edge cases in the physical world and can articulate architectural trade-offs to drive the best system-level decisions.

  • Nice to have: Experience with optimization libraries (Ceres Solver, GTSAM), parallel computing (CUDA), Docker, and PCL.

  • Location Requirement: This role is on-site at our HQ, working directly with the physical sensor rigs and robots.

About Us
At Pickle Robot, we're on a mission to automate global supply chains with Physical AI. Our robots work alongside warehouse teams to unload trucks and containers — one of the toughest, most understaffed jobs in logistics — making the work safer, faster, and more efficient for the people doing it.  Loading trucks comes next, followed by the Dill Autonomy Engine: generalized autonomy that will eventually orchestrate robots across entire logistics processes.


We're looking for a Software Engineer to join our Task & Motion Planning team, which decides what our robots pick, how they grasp it, and how they move safely and quickly through a cluttered, changing trailer. We're looking for someone who brings strong software engineering fundamentals, a track record of shipping production code, and a genuine interest in motion planning and grasping.
You'll design and build fast, reliable, well-tested planning systems that run on real robots every day. Your code will directly affect how many boxes come off a truck per hour and how often a robot needs a human's help, and you'll see those results on the warehouse floor.

lists.content:
• Design, build, and maintain production C++ and Python components of our planning stack, including motion planning, grasp selection, collision checking, and task sequencing

  • Take algorithms, your own and your teammates', from prototype to deployment, owning the architecture, performance, and robustness of the implementation

  • Profile and optimize performance-critical code so planners meet real-time cycle-time targets on robot hardware

  • Build the testing, simulation, and benchmarking infrastructure that lets the team change planning code with confidence

  • Improve the reliability of the planning stack in the field by debugging failures from production logs, building tooling for triage, and fixing root causes

  • Help raise the bar for code quality through design reviews, code reviews, and good engineering practices

• 2–4 years of experience writing and shipping production software, primarily in modern C++ (C++17 or later), with working proficiency in Python

  • Strong fundamentals in software design, data structures, algorithms, and performance optimization

  • Experience owning components end-to-end: design, implementation, testing, deployment, and ongoing support

  • Solid understanding of concurrency, memory management, and profiling tools

  • A real interest in motion planning, manipulation, and grasping, and eagerness to go deep on the algorithms alongside domain experts

  • Comfort working close to hardware and debugging problems that span software and the physical world

    • Nice to Have

  • Hands-on experience with motion planning or manipulation (e.g., sampling-based or optimization-based planners, trajectory generation, grasp planning)

  • Experience with CUDA or GPU performance optimization

  • Familiarity with robotics libraries and frameworks such as OMPL, Drake, FCL, or Pinocchio

  • Background in 3D geometry, kinematics, or linear algebra (Eigen or similar)

  • Experience with simulation environments and large-scale regression testing for robotics or other safety-critical systems

  • Experience deploying software on physical robots in production environments
